title: Prefill/Decode Latency Steering Fabric and Adaptive Kernel Hints
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: As we scale multi-GPU serving for longer context models, observed 95th/99th token latency regressions are correlated with poor overlap between NCCL communication windows and compute kernels, and suboptimal kernel choices for short vs long sequence workloads. This ticket implements a low-risk "steering fabric" that dynamically routes token-wavelets and exposes adaptive kernel hints to the runtime to improve overlap and reduce tail latency without increasing average token cost.
background: Recent customer incidents and internal bench runs show spiky tails at decode when heterogeneous request sizes hit the same pipeline stage. Existing heuristics pick kernels based on static model profile and average seq length, which misses micro-distributions in production traffic (e.g., 60% short prefill, 30% long streaming, 10% burst prefills). NCCL windows frequently misalign with short-window compute, causing idle comm periods and queueing in later stages.
proposal_summary: Introduce a steering layer that: 1) samples the sequence-length distribution per token-wave and tags microbatches with a fast/normal class; 2) emits lightweight kernel hints (quantized: FAST|BALANCED|THOROUGH) and an NCCL overlap preference to the conductor; 3) enables opportunistic rendezvous windows by nudging comm start times within a configured slack; 4) adds a runtime path for short-prefill fast kernels that prioritize lower latency at slight throughput cost.
design_decisions: Keep steering logic in serving runtime (no control-plane dependency) to ensure sub-ms decisions.
Use 3-point kernel hint enumeration instead of continuous score to keep planner simple and debuggable.
Do not change kernel implementations now; route only to existing kernels and microbatch size/shaping to validate gains first.
Make NCCL overlap adjustments bounded by per-stage slack to avoid cascading delays under sustained load.
Expose all steering decisions via trace headers for post-hoc analysis and reproducibility.
acceptance_criteria: 95th token latency reduced by >= 12% on representative mixed-short-long trace in staging across TPxPP configs
No regression (>3%) in tokens-per-second for heavy long-prefill synthetic benchmark
Telemetry exposes per-wave kernel_hint, chosen_kernel, comm_start_offset_ms, and overlap_ratio; dashboards show alignment improvement
Feature gated behind runtime flag 'steering.fabric.v1' and covered by unit+integration tests
Canary rollout plan documented and automated in console rollout job
implementation_notes: Phases: (A) telemetry + tagging (safe read-only) to collect sequence-wave histograms; (B) steering fabric that emits kernel_hint and comm_slack directives; (C) conductor integration to apply kernel_hint and adjust rendezvous timing; (D) canary rollout and telemetry SLO checks. Start with 1xTP2xPP config then expand.
benchmarks: Preliminary microbench in lab: mixed 16/512 seq distribution on 4-GPU A100, baseline 95th=42ms, with prototype steering 95th=34ms, avg throughput -1.8%. More comprehensive runs required across mGPU topologies.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal staging: feature flag true on 10% of requests for non-critical routes (2 days); 2) Canary: enable on dedicated capacity pools for customers on test accounts (1 week); 3) Gradual ramp with SLO guardrails and auto rollback if 95th increases >5% or throughput drops >6%.
telemetry_and_observability: New traces: 'steering.hint', 'steering.comm_offset_ms', 'steering.overlap_score'. Dashboard 'Steering Fabric — overlap & latency' and alert if per-route overlap_score falls below 0.45 or if kernel_hint mispredict rate >8%.

notes: Trade-offs: prioritizing tail latency for short prefills may reduce peak throughput; gating via feature flag and per-pool policies mitigates customer impact. Goal is to make decisions reversible and observable so we can tune kernel hints over time.
qa_test_plan: Unit tests for hint propagation, integration tests for conductor applying hints, e2e validation using production-replay traces, and chaos tests where comm windows are artificially delayed.
estimated_cost_impact: Expect marginal increase in GPU cycles for short-prefill paths, estimated +1-3% cost for routes using FAST hint; savings come from reduced tail-induced overprovisioning.
